aspect: The scale of the shortage, stated by the regulator's own side
description: About 800 pharmaceutical products in short supply nationwide, including 90 classed as essential and life-saving, per the Iranian Pharmacists Association spokesman.
energy_note: Ninety life-saving drugs, absent, at once.

aspect: The humanitarian exemption does not function
description: Medicine is formally exempt. Restrictions on banking, shipping and insurance mean importers cannot pay for or transport it, so the exemption exists on paper while the shelf is empty.
source_name: Peer-reviewed: health service disruption under sanctions

aspect: It reaches the patient as delay, substitution and death
description: A qualitative study of Iranian cancer care found sanctions restricted access to standard equipment and modern technology, producing delays, misdiagnosis and diagnostic and therapeutic side effects 'to the point of death'. Some patients discontinued treatment entirely.

aspect: Currency allocation is the real rationing mechanism
description: After the UN snapback, about USD 3.4bn was allocated for medicines and equipment, and hard-currency availability had already cut effective access to that funding by 10 to 20 percent. The rationing is done by exchange rate, invisibly.
money_note: Patient-side cost of drugs bought at unofficial rates.
energy_note: Rationed by a number on a screen in another country.

aspect: The psychological effect is specific: it is being slowly told you do not count
description: Unlike a strike, sanctions produce no single moment and no image. The message received over years is that the suffering of the population is an acceptable instrument, which corrodes something different from fear.
energy_note: Not terror. A long, formal insult.

aspect: SCENARIO - the MS patient and the three pharmacies
description: Her interferon has been unavailable for five weeks. The pharmacist suggests a domestic substitute he cannot vouch for, at four times last year's price, in a currency that lost a third of its value since her last prescription. She takes it, because the alternative is nothing.
energy_note: Injecting something you hope is the same drug.

aspect: SECONDARY - it makes the population blame itself
description: Shortage is experienced as domestic failure - corruption, incompetence, hoarding - which is also partly true. The result is a population angry at itself about a condition imposed from outside, which is politically useful to everyone except the population.
energy_note: Furious at the wrong people, correctly.

aspect: How this dataset relates to the other two
description: assets/text/general lists what is imposed on anyone. assets/text/iran lists what is imposed on top by nationality and status. This file lists what is imposed on top of that by war, in whatever form it is being conducted. They are additive: an Iranian under sanctions queues for medicine (here), proves identity to a visa officer (iran), and waits on hold to a call centre that cannot help (general), in the same week.
energy_note: Three stacked queues, in the same week, for one person.
notes: Read the three listissue.csv files side by side; the schemas are aligned.
